Prunely Privacy Policy

Effective October 8, 2026 · Last updated October 8, 2026

The short version. Prunely looks at your photo library on your iPhone and never uploads your photos. There is no account and we run no server for the app. Purchases go through Apple. The free version shows ads, and the ad companies collect some device data to show them; you control tracking with Apple's prompt and the in-app privacy choices, and Pro removes ads entirely.

Who we are

Prunely is made by an independent developer ("we", "us"). This policy covers the Prunely iPhone app, its widgets and Shortcuts. If you have a question, email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Your photos

With your permission (Apple's Photos access prompt), Prunely reads your photo library so it can:

  • show your photos and videos as cards to keep, delete, favorite, skip or sort into albums;
  • measure file sizes, and find screenshots, large videos, Live Photos, bursts, duplicates, similar shots and blurry photos;
  • when you confirm, delete items, mark favorites or add items to albums in the Photos app.

All of this happens on your iPhone. Image analysis (finding similar or blurry photos) uses Apple's on-device frameworks. Your photos, videos, their contents and their metadata (dates, locations, faces) are never uploaded to us or anyone else, and are never given to ad SDKs.

If you choose Limited Access, Prunely only sees the photos you select. You can change access at any time in Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Prunely.

When you delete items, iOS shows its own confirmation, then moves them to the Photos app's Recently Deleted album, where they stay for up to 30 days before iOS removes them for good. Prunely never deletes anything without that confirmation.

Data stored on your device

To remember your progress, Prunely saves the following in its private storage on your iPhone:

  • your decisions (kept, staged for deletion, favorited, sorted), keyed by the Photos item's on-device identifier, with its size and date;
  • daily activity, goals, streaks and cleaned-space totals;
  • an image-analysis cache (numeric "fingerprints" and sharpness scores, not copies of your photos);
  • settings such as your daily goal, reminder time and pinned albums;
  • a small summary for widgets (for example "3.4 GB cleaned" and your streak), never photos or identifiers;
  • two numbers in your iPhone's Keychain recording how much you have deleted under the free allowance, so the allowance stays fair after a reinstall. This stays on your device (and in your own encrypted backups) and is not synced to iCloud Keychain.

This data never leaves your device except inside your own iPhone backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup), which Apple and you control. We cannot access it.

iCloud Photos

Prunely has no iCloud sync of its own. If you use iCloud Photos with "Optimize iPhone Storage", some originals live in your iCloud. When you view such an item, iOS downloads it from your iCloud account to your iPhone, as the Photos app does. You can turn these downloads off in Prunely's Settings. We never see this traffic or your iCloud account.

With iCloud Photos on, deleting a photo also removes it from your other devices and any Shared Library. Prunely reminds you of this before you confirm.

Network connections

Prunely itself operates no server. The app connects to the internet only for:

  • Apple's App Store: loading prices, purchases, restores and subscription status.
  • iCloud Photos downloads, made by iOS as described above (optional).
  • Apple Maps place names (off by default). City names come from a list built into the app. If you turn on "Place names from Apple Maps" in Prunely's Privacy settings, photo coordinates are sent to Apple to look up a place name. Apple's handling is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.
  • Ads in the free version (see Advertising). These requests contain device data, not your photos.

You can check this yourself with iOS's App Privacy Report (Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report).

Notifications and widgets

Reminders (daily tidy, trial-end reminder) are local notifications scheduled on your iPhone; they are not sent through any server. Widgets and Live Activities show totals such as space cleaned and your streak, read from your device.

Purchases and subscriptions

Prunely Pro is sold through Apple's App Store using StoreKit. Apple handles the payment, your payment details, your Apple ID and your billing address. We never see your name, email address or payment information. The app only receives a signed confirmation from Apple saying which product is active (for example, "Yearly, renews on a date" or "Lifetime") so it can unlock Pro and switch off ads. That check happens on your device. Apple's handling of purchase data is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

App Store Connect gives us aggregated, non-identifying sales reports (for example, how many trials started in a country). Apple does not give us your identity.

Advertising in the free version

The free version of Prunely shows ads. Buying Prunely Pro (a subscription or the lifetime purchase) removes all ads, and the ad SDK then stops requesting ads.

Ads are delivered by AppLovin MAX, an ad mediation SDK built into the app. MAX may fill an ad slot from AppLovin itself or from other ad networks it mediates, such as Google AdMob. These companies, not us, receive and process the data described below. We do not receive it in a form that identifies you; we only see aggregated reports such as how many ads were shown and how much they earned.

What the ad SDKs may collect

DataWhenUsed for
Advertising identifier (IDFA)Only if you tap "Allow" on Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt. If you choose "Ask App Not to Track", iOS gives the SDK an all-zeros identifier instead.Personalized ads, measuring ads across apps (tracking)
Identifier for Vendor (IDFV) and SDK-generated IDsWhenever an ad is requestedFrequency capping, fraud prevention, reporting; not linked across companies' apps without your permission
IP address and approximate (coarse) location derived from itWhenever an ad is requestedDelivering ads, picking the right language/region, legal compliance (for example, privacy rules by region), fraud prevention
Device and app information: device model, iOS version, language, time zone, screen size, network type, carrier, app name and versionWhenever an ad is requestedShowing ads that fit your device, troubleshooting, fraud prevention
Ad interaction data: which ads were shown, taps, video completions, rewarded-ad completionsWhen you see or interact with an adAd delivery, measurement, billing between ad companies, rewarding you for a rewarded ad
Ad SDK diagnostics (crash and performance data about the ad SDK)If the ad SDK has a problemKeeping the ad SDK working

Ad SDKs never get access to your photos, videos, albums, swipe decisions or cleanup statistics. Those stay on your iPhone and are never shared with ad partners, and they are not used to choose which ads you see.

The app does not request precise location for ads and does not give ad SDKs access to your contacts, camera, microphone or Health data.

Your ad choices

  • App Tracking Transparency (all users). The first time ads might be personalized, the app explains why and then shows Apple's prompt. Choose "Ask App Not to Track" and the ad SDKs cannot use your IDFA or track you across other companies' apps and websites; you will still see ads, but they are non-personalized or based on the content of the app. You can change this at any time in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking (per app, or turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track" for every app).
  • In-app consent manager (EEA, UK, Switzerland and US states with privacy laws). Where the law requires it, a consent screen (Google's User Messaging Platform, shown through AppLovin MAX) asks before any data is used for personalized ads, and lets you accept, reject or pick partners and purposes. You can reopen it at any time from Prunely Settings > Ad Privacy Choices to change or withdraw your consent, or to opt out of the "sale" or "sharing" of personal information for targeted advertising.
  • Remove ads entirely by buying Prunely Pro. A subscription or lifetime purchase turns off all ads.
  • Limit ad personalization at the partner. Google: My Ad Center.

Ad partners and their privacy policies

  • AppLovin (MAX mediation and AppLovin ads): applovin.com/privacy
  • Google AdMob: Google Privacy Policy and How Google uses information from apps that use its services

We may add or remove mediated ad networks over time. When we add one, we will list it here and update the changelog at the bottom of this page. The full, current list of partners and purposes is also shown in the consent screen where that screen applies.

What we never do

  • No account, sign-in or email address needed.
  • No uploading, scanning or "AI analysis" of your photos in the cloud.
  • No analytics or crash-reporting SDKs of our own. (Ad SDKs may report their own diagnostics, as described above.)
  • We do not sell your photos or app data, and we never use them for advertising.

Data retention

  • On-device app data is kept until you reset it or delete the app (see below). We keep no copy.
  • Deleted photos stay in the Photos app's Recently Deleted album for up to 30 days, or until you empty it.
  • Ad data is retained by AppLovin, Google and other ad partners according to their own policies linked above.
  • Purchase records are kept by Apple under Apple's policies.
  • Support emails you send us are kept only as long as needed to help you and keep a record of the conversation, then deleted, normally within 24 months. Ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Deleting your data

  • Reset your progress: Prunely Settings > "Review everything again" clears decisions that haven't been committed.
  • Delete everything: delete the Prunely app. iOS removes its data, widgets and reminders. Only the two-number free-allowance counter in the Keychain remains on the device; it contains no photos or personal details.
  • Ad data: use the choices in Your ad choices, or contact the ad partner directly. You can also email us and we will help you reach them.

Your privacy rights

Because Prunely has no account and no server, we do not hold a profile about you. Your app data is on your device, where you can view, export (where the app offers it) and delete it yourself. For data the ad partners collect, you can use the choices above or contact the partner directly. Whatever your location, you can email us and we will help.

EEA, UK and Switzerland (GDPR / UK GDPR)

  • Who is responsible. We, the developer of Prunely, are the controller for the limited personal data we handle (for example, emails you send us, and the decision to integrate ad SDKs). AppLovin, Google and other ad partners act as independent controllers for the data they collect to deliver and measure ads.
  • Legal bases. Personalized ads and the access to device identifiers they need: your consent, collected through the consent screen and Apple's tracking prompt. Showing non-personalized ads, frequency capping, fraud prevention and security: the legitimate interests of the developer of Prunely and the ad partners in funding a free app and keeping ads safe. Replying to your support email: our legitimate interest in helping you (or steps you ask for before a contract). Purchases: handled by Apple under Apple's terms.
  • Your rights. Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection (including to processing based on legitimate interests), data portability, and withdrawing consent at any time without affecting earlier processing. Withdraw ad consent in Prunely Settings > Ad Privacy Choices; object or ask about anything else by emailing SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.
  • Complaints. You can complain to your local data protection authority. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.
  • International transfers. Ad partners may process data in the United States and other countries. They rely on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and, where they are certified, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; see their policies above.

California and other US states (CCPA / CPRA and similar laws)

  • Categories collected in the last 12 months (by ad partners through the free version only): identifiers (IDFA with your permission, IDFV, SDK IDs, IP address); internet or other electronic network activity (ad impressions and taps); approximate geolocation derived from IP; device information. Inferences may be drawn by ad partners for personalized ads if you allow it. We do not collect sensitive personal information, and your in-app data is never shared with ad partners.
  • Sources and purposes. Collected directly from your device by the ad SDKs, for the advertising, measurement, security and fraud-prevention purposes described above.
  • "Sale" and "sharing". We do not sell personal information for money. Letting ad partners use identifiers for cross-context behavioral advertising may count as "selling" or "sharing" under California law. To opt out: choose "Ask App Not to Track", and/or open Prunely Settings > Ad Privacy Choices and opt out of sale/sharing, or email us. You can also buy Pro to remove ads entirely.
  • Your rights. To know/access, delete, correct, opt out of sale or sharing, and limit the use of sensitive personal information (we do not use any). We will not discriminate against you for using these rights; the free version stays the same whether or not you opt out. An authorized agent may make a request on your behalf with your written permission. Because we hold no account data, we may not be able to link ad-partner data to you; we will tell you which partner to contact and how.
  • Retention. See Data retention.
  • Minors. We do not knowingly sell or share the personal information of consumers under 16.

Residents of other US states with consumer privacy laws (for example Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas and Oregon) have similar rights to access, delete, correct and opt out of targeted advertising. Use the same steps above or email us. If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying to our answer with "Appeal" in the subject line.

Children

Prunely is rated 4+ on the App Store because it has no objectionable content, but it is a general-audience utility and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country). If you believe a child has provided personal information to us, for example by email, contact us and we will delete it. Parents can prevent in-app purchases with Screen Time and Ask to Buy, and can turn off tracking in Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.

Security

Your app data is protected by iOS app sandboxing and Data Protection encryption on your device. Because we don't operate a server or collect your data, there is no developer-held database of your information that could be breached. No method of storage is perfect, so keep your device passcode and Apple ID secure.

Contact

Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD for questions, privacy requests or complaints. If you email us, we receive your email address and whatever you write, and use it only to reply. We aim to answer within 7 days, and privacy requests within the time the law requires (30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA).

Changes and changelog

If we change how Prunely handles data, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect, and for significant changes we will tell you in the app. The App Store privacy label is kept in line with this page.
